resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower is used on very high fire danger days; Wikipedia's list says it is used on high wind days. Both are reported in the story. Neither was confirmed by an agency source in this research.

sources.title: List of fire lookout towers in Louisiana

notes_for_editor: No build year, first-staffing date, or move/alteration history was found in the sources reached, so the story says so. The record's elevation (27.1 m) is consistent with the register's 89 ft. The 33.5 m height is converted from the register's 110 ft. Access is unknown: no source reached says whether the public may visit, so no access or visit fact is written. Use wording conflicts between the register (very high fire danger days) and Wikipedia (high wind days); the Wikipedia asterisk is unexplained. Do not confuse with a Gordon tower in Wisconsin (a 1935 Aermotor listing seen in a search result, T.44N-R.12W); that is a different structure and was excluded. An OpenStreetMap node (358380019) tags it as an observation tower of lattice construction at ~26 m, but that was not cited. Search budget: three websearch.py calls, one over the two-per-tower budget.
